scenarios.name: cold_with_frost_protection_off
scenarios.description: The motivating case: -15 C outdoor air, the ERV running, and the frost sequence reporting inactive. All three conjuncts hold from t=0, so delayOnInit makes the alarm land one alarm_delay (300 s) in.

scenarios.name: cold_with_frost_protection_engaged
scenarios.description: Same -15 C outdoor air with the frost sequence engaged. This is the unit working as designed and the rule stays silent no matter how cold it gets.

scenarios.name: mild_outdoor_air_no_frost_protection
scenarios.description: -2 C with frost protection off. Frost protection is not supposed to be running here — the threshold is what separates a missing sequence from a sequence that has no reason to act.

scenarios.name: erv_disabled_in_deep_cold
scenarios.description: -20 C, frost protection off, but the ERV is not enabled: no air is moving through the core, so there is nothing to frost. The enable conjunct holds yFault down — and false here means 'not applicable', not 'protected'.

scenarios.name: oat_exactly_at_frost_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary: outdoor air sitting exactly on frost_threshold (-10.0 C) with frost protection off. CDL Reals has no LessEqual, so the comparison is strict `<` and exactly -10.0 clears.

scenarios.name: oat_just_below_frost_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary from the other side: -10.1 C, one tenth of a degree colder than the threshold. The cold term now passes and the alarm lands after alarm_delay.

scenarios.name: brief_cold_excursion
scenarios.description: A three-minute dip to -12 C with frost protection off, ending 120 s short of the 300 s alarm_delay. The timer resets when the air warms and no alarm is ever raised.

scenarios.name: frost_protection_engages_after_alarm
scenarios.description: Recovery: the alarm asserts at 300 s, then the frost sequence starts at t=900 s. yFault drops on that same tick — TrueDelay only delays the rising edge — even though the outdoor air is still at -15 C.

scenarios.name: erv_shuts_down_after_alarm
scenarios.description: The other release path: the alarm asserts at 300 s and the ERV is disabled at t=900 s. yFault drops with the enable, which is the reference's own semantics — the fault describes an enabled ERV running unprotected.
